## 0a. OFFICIAL DTCG 2025.10 SCHEMA VALIDATION — I-08B3.1-B4R

Kept **separate from QANDEEL's own validation** on purpose. B4 validated its resolver document
with a checker B4 wrote, against a shape B4 believed; both agreed and both were wrong. A validator
authored beside the artefact cannot discover that its model of the standard is mistaken.

**Authority:** `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/`, vendored from `https://github.com/design-tokens/community-group`,
22 schema files, dialect draft-07. Report pinned to publication
commit `f0f32a7dce0b (2025-10-28, "Publish 2025.10" #340)`; schema sources at `11f95e87701e (2026-06-09, "Bundle JSON schema" #412) - the last commit to touch schemas/src/2025.10/resolver*`.
Retrieved 2026-09-21. **Validator: `ajv`** — third party, not authored here.

| check | result | detail |
|---|---|---|
| **S-01** The vendored official schemas are unaltered | PASS | 22 schema files re-hashed; SHA-256 and git blob SHA-1 both match `PROVENANCE.json`; 22 of 22 blob shas were verified at vendoring time against the shas the GitHub tree API reports for the official repository; 0 unrecorded files present |
| **S-02** The resolver document is VALID against the official DTCG 2025.10 Resolver Schema | PASS | valid against `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/resolver.json` (draft-07, resolved through its 3 sub-schemas), validated by ajv - a third-party implementation this package did not author |
| **S-03** Every shipped token file is VALID against the official DTCG 2025.10 Format Schema | PASS | 6 token files valid against `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/format.json`, including the two value-free appearance sets and the canonical deliverable |
| **S-04** The document declares the schema it is actually valid against | PASS | `$schema` is `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/resolver.json`, and that id is the `$id` of the vendored file `schemas/2025.10/resolver.json` which S-02 validated against |

the 6 probes are **accepted by the official schema and rejected only by V-11**

**What each probe is:**

- `n1` → INV-02 — The duplication the brief names by name: an ASIDE given its own copy of the same hex. Every colour comparison in the world still passes on this document. Only the chain knows.
- `n2` → INV-01 — The most natural way a second tone actually arrives: not by decision, but by someone needing "the one that sits on top" and adding it. Note that this probe is what proved the first definition of the Surface family circular - see `context()`.
- `n3` → INV-04 — A tint of exactly one 8-bit step on one channel - the smallest chromatic Surface that can exist, and the one a designer would never see.
- `n4` → INV-05 — A sunken Surface: darker than the World it sits on. B1 retired the direction; this is what it would look like arriving through the token file.
- `n5` → INV-06 — A scrim on an ASIDE - the failure B0R froze the rule against, expressed as a token.
- `n6` → INV-11 — The retired translucency diagnostic reinstated as production truth. It keeps the canonical hex, so INV-03 is silent and only the alpha gives it away.
- `n7` → INV-03 — A retired B2 value back in the output. Assembled from halves so this probe does not itself plant the needle the scan hunts.
- `n8` → INV-12 — An appearance hard-coded into an appearance-independent name - exactly what forces a component rewrite when Light arrives. THIS PROBE FOUND A REAL HOLE: under whole-segment matching, `functionalDark` did not contain the word `dark`, INV-12 stayed silent, and the suite would have passed on INV-01 alone.
- `n9` → INV-09 — A brand accent quietly taking control of the Surface - the system dying by derivation rather than by decision, which is how it would actually die.
- `n10` → INV-08 — A Surface that encodes an analytical property - SG-1 broken at the token layer, where it is cheapest to break and hardest to see.
- `n11` → INV-07 — The nesting step itself: an ASIDE over a PASSAGE given its own slightly lighter tone, which is what every elevation system in the world would do here and what B0R forbade.
- `n12` → INV-10 — Material 3's mechanism arriving as metadata rather than as a token: an extension that tells a build step how to derive a lighter Surface from an elevation level. No name changes, no value changes, and the one-tone rule is over.

## 5. B4.4 — Scrim production verification

**One value verified: neutral black at alpha 0.5, read out of the token file.**
Not a search. Every measurement is against a prediction computed from CSS Color 4 alpha
compositing **before** anything was rendered — a measurement with no prediction in front of it can
only agree with itself.

| measurement | predicted | measured | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| World fill, live | `#101010` | `#101010` | PASS |
| World fill, suppressed | `#080808` | `#080808` | PASS |
| APPARATUS fill, live | `#181818` | `#181818` | PASS |
| APPARATUS fill, suppressed | `#0c0c0c` | `#0c0c0c` | PASS |
| PASSAGE fill (foreground) | `#181818` | `#181818` | PASS |

### The named criteria

| criterion | result |
|---|---|
| World is perceptually suppressed | **YES** — luminance falls to 50.0% of live; the World fill composites exactly to `#080808` |
| orientation remains sufficient | **YES** — the suspended World keeps 229 distinct levels (live: 381); structure survives rather than flattening |
| PASSAGE foreground remains clear | **YES** — primary reading on the PASSAGE measures 12.083:1 |
| Surface `#181818` remains stable | **YES** — the PASSAGE fill measures `#181818`, unchanged |
| no role-specific Surface change is needed | **YES** — one tone throughout; INV-01 and the N2 composition both hold |
| focus / modality truth unaffected | **YES** — the static focus topology is identical between the model-driven and token-driven renders of every composition |
| background legibility | **NOT A PASS CRITERION** — see below |

### Two figures that need their framing stated

**Reading behind the scrim falls 12.95:1 → 3.75:1.** This is reported and is **not** a pass
criterion. The Design Director's D-5 direction is that the scrim expresses WORLD SUPPRESSION
rather than preserving background-reading eligibility. The World behind a PASSAGE is suspended, so
text still legible there is not a benefit and text that is not is not a defect.

**The PASSAGE panel measures 1.128:1 against the suspended World** (it would be 1.072:1 without the scrim —
the scrim improves the boundary by a factor of 1.053).
That separation is small, and it is supposed to be: the frozen mechanism for telling a PASSAGE
apart is **occlusion plus a uniform scrim plus modal behaviour**, not edge contrast. A one-tone
system that separated by edge contrast would need a second tone, which is the whole B-track
reopening. **If a later accessibility expression requires this boundary to clear SC 1.4.11's 3:1,
the answer is a Class S structural line on the PASSAGE, and its colour is explicitly not B4's to
choose.** Recorded as an open dependency, not resolved here.

**The scrim does not fail.** No contradiction was found, and no other alpha was tried.

## 6. Stop conditions

| condition | triggered? |
|---|---|
| `#181818` cannot be represented as one shared semantic token | NO — INV-01: four roles, one source, chain length 3 |
| the selected 50% scrim fails the accepted PASSAGE integration | NO — 5/5 measurements match prediction exactly |
| role-specific Surface values become necessary | NO — one tone survived every composition including N2 |
| a Light value must be invented | NO — the Light set contributes 0 values and the absence is detectable (V-09) |
| a final Class S / focus colour must be invented | NO — neither is in the token file; both deferred to E/F |
| frozen A/B doctrine must be reopened | NO — no A or B conclusion is changed |
| production mapping requires Material tonalElevation | NO — explicitly not inherited; INV-10 makes it a failing test |
| Product roles would need to become platform accessibility roles | NO — B3R's separation is carried forward intact |
| token validation cannot enforce the one-tone invariant | NO — enforced structurally on alias chains, and probe `n1` proves it catches four equal hexes |
| Skill Gate or Reference Gate cannot be verified | NO — both verified; failures and substitutions recorded |
| **B4R:** the official schema and the custom validator disagree | NO — S-05 PASS. On the shipped document both accept; on probes they partition, and 0 probe(s) escaped both |
| **B4R:** correcting the resolver changes a resolved dark value or the alias topology | NO — all six token files byte-identical to B4; V-06 still reports 1 literal and 6 tokens reaching it by reference |

**No stop condition was triggered.**
